parts.text: In this experiment, you will investigate the resistance of a wire. Refer to Figure 2.1. The circuit has been set up for you.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (a) (i) Close the switch. Measure the current I 1 in the circuit. Include the unit. I 1 = .................................. unit ............... [1]

ms.label: 2(a)(i)
ms.text: I1 to at least 2 decimal places and < 1 A

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Measure the potential difference (p.d.) V 1 across the resistance wire connected between B and C. Include the unit. V 1 = .................................. unit ............... [1] Open the switch.

ms.label: 2(a)(ii)
ms.text: V1 to at least 1 decimal place and < 3 V

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Calculate the resistance R 1 of the resistance wire using the equation: R 1 = V 1 I 1 . R 1 = ...................................................... Ω [1]

ms.label: 2(a)(iii)
ms.text: R1 present and units A and V

parts.label: iv
parts.text: (iv) The length of the resistance wire is 50 cm. Calculate r, the resistance per cm of the resistance wire, using the equation: r = R 1 50 cm . r = ............................................... Ω / cm [1]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) You are provided with a length of the same resistance wire wound on a wooden rod.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Record the number of whole turns N of wire on the rod. N = ............................................................... Measure the diameter d of the rod. Give your answer in centimetres to the nearest millimetre. d = .......................................................... cm [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate a value l 1 for the length of wire on the rod using the equation: l 1 = Nπd. l 1 = .................................................... cm [1]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Disconnect the voltmeter from the circuit. Disconnect the resistance wire from B and C. Connect the wire on the rod to the circuit at B and C. Do not remove the wire from the rod. Connect the voltmeter across BC.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Close the switch. Measure the current I 2 in the circuit. I 2 = ............................................................... Measure the potential difference (p.d.) V 2 across the resistance wire on the rod. V 2 = ............................................................... [1] Open the switch.

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate the resistance R 2 of the resistance wire on the rod using the equation: R 2 = V 2 I 2 . R 2 = ...................................................... Ω [1]

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) Calculate another value l 2 for the length of resistance wire on the rod using your values from 2(a)(iv) and 2(c)(ii) and the equation: l 2 = R 2 r . Give your answer in centimetres to the nearest millimetre. l 2 = .................................................... cm [1]

ms.label: 2(d)
ms.text: l2 in range 40 to 60 cm and to nearest mm

ms.label: 2(e)
ms.text:
Suitable reason (that matches suggestion)
Sensible comparison with other method
